pairs.old: By 2023, approximately 72% of Medicaid beneficiaries — and 55% of Medicaid spending — flows through managed care organizations (MCOs).
pairs.new: By July 2024, about 78% of Medicaid enrollees were in comprehensive managed care organizations (MCOs) (CMS), and payments to MCOs made up about 52% of total Medicaid spending in FY 2023 (KFF).
pairs.claim: By 2023 ~72% of beneficiaries and 55% of spending flow through MCOs
pairs.src: CMS 2024 Medicaid Managed Care Enrollment report (fetched PDF): 78.2% in comprehensive MCOs; KFF: MCO payments ~52% of total Medicaid spending FY2023

pairs.old: MCOs must spend at least 85% of premium revenue on medical costs (medical loss ratio). Excess profit must be returned to the state.
pairs.new: States must set capitation rates so each MCO can reasonably achieve a medical loss ratio of at least 85%; states may require plans that fall short to remit the difference.
pairs.claim: MCOs must spend 85%; excess profit must be returned to the state
pairs.src: 42 CFR 438.4(b)(9) and 438.8 (85% MLR standard for rate setting; remittance is a state option per 438.8(j)); MACPAC MLR issue brief Jan 2022

pairs.old: Several Republican administrations approved 1115 waivers requiring Medicaid enrollees to document work, volunteering, or job training to maintain coverage. Courts repeatedly struck these down, ruling that work requirements do not promote Medicaid's objective of providing health coverage — they undermine it by causing coverage loss. The legal and policy debate continues.
pairs.new: The first Trump administration approved 1115 waivers requiring some Medicaid enrollees to document work, volunteering, or job training to keep coverage. Federal courts set several approvals aside — in Gresham v. Azar (D.C. Cir., 2020) the court held that HHS had failed to weigh the waivers' effect on coverage, Medicaid's central objective. In July 2025, Congress put community-engagement requirements for expansion adults into federal law (P.L. 119-21), taking effect January 1, 2027.
pairs.claim: Several Republican administrations approved work requirements; courts repeatedly struck them down; debate continues (stale: omits 2025 statute)
pairs.src: Gresham v. Azar, 950 F.3d 93 (D.C. Cir. 2020); P.L. 119-21 signed July 4, 2025 (NACo, CRS R48755): community engagement for expansion adults 19-64 from Jan 1, 2027

pairs.old: Work requirements: blocked by the courts
pairs.new: Work requirements: from the courts to federal law

pairs.old: Require documentation of employment or community engagement — legally contested and often blocked.
pairs.new: Require documentation of employment or community engagement — contested in court, then written into federal law for expansion adults in 2025.
